newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong dips again, Thai hits 40-month low.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong dips again, Thai hits 40-month low.

text.p: Hong Kong shares closed weaker for the second day on Wednesday as investors continued to take profit. In Bangkok, shares ended at their lowest level in 40 months, and Bombay stocks fell to another three-year low.
Most other major Asian markets had a quiet day.

Tokyo stocks ended up 0.14 percent in directionless trade. Australia fell 0.39 percent, Taiwan rose 0.10 percent, Singapore up 0.40 percent and Malaysia gained 0.47 percent. In Tokyo, shares ended mixed with the key Nikkei 225 average edging up 29.35 points to finish at 20,659.91.
Brokers said after an initial dip at the open on Wall Street's losses, buying was limited to selected blue-chip issues, while the recent fall in other issues lost momentum.
"No fresh money seemed to flow into the market, and I expect the downside to become vulnerable," said Masaaki Higashida, strategist at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Analysts in Hong Kong said cautious market sentiment drove stocks to a weaker close, but laggard chasing and bargain-hunting allowed prices to finish off their lows.
The Hang Seng index closed with a loss of 22.02 points at 13,434.24, off its intraday low of 13,344.80. Turnover was a busy HK$8.61 billion, up on Tuesday's HK$7.51 billion.

"It seems that the market right now is kind of in a consolidation phase," said Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities. He said losses on Wall Street overnight had dampened local market sentiment.

Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities said: "Because we have not seen a major move in the price of the (U.S. long) bond, I think probably there is every reason we are going to hold at these levels."
However, he added: "Whether this can actually be sustained if Wall Street continues to come lower is questionable."
Traders in Bangkok said selling by foreigners and fears of a major foreign exodus from the bourse pulled Thai stocks to their lowest level in 40 months.
The SET Index shed 7.49 points, or 0.83 percent, to close below the 900-point level at 898.32, on trade worth 3.53 billion baht. The previous lowest close was 893.14 on July 27, 1993.

"The first worry is the government's ability to deal with the economy, but the other is that people are worried foreign mutual funds might leave the market," said an analyst at Pacific Finance and Securities.

In Bombay, selling of blue-chip stocks pulled the market down to another three-year low. The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) 30-share index shed 85 points in mid-session and ended 48.59 points down, or 1.74 percent, at a provisional 2,749.41.
At 1112 GMT, the dollar traded at 113.13/23 yen and 1.5590/95 marks.
Gold finished slightly firmer in Hong Kong at US$368.60/369.10 an ounce, up from New York's $368.40/90 close on Tuesday.
SIMEX Brent crude futures traded lower late on Wednesday.
January futures last traded at $23.60 per barrel, down 17 cents from London's settlement of $23.77.
